# Yes, Everything Gets Deleted

When you run `pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name>`, it **completely removes the entire virtual environment directory**, which includes:

- ✅ All installed packages (pip-installed libraries)
- ✅ The Python interpreter copy/link for that venv
- ✅ All configuration files (`pyvenv.cfg`, etc.)
- ✅ The `site-packages` directory
- ✅ Any scripts/binaries installed by packages

## What it does NOT delete:

- ❌ Your project source code
- ❌ The base Python version installed via pyenv
- ❌ Other virtual environments
- ❌ Your `requirements.txt` or `pyproject.toml` files

## Tip: Save your dependencies first

If you want to recreate the environment later, export your packages before deleting:

```bash
pyenv activate <venv-name>
pip freeze > requirements.txt
pyenv deactivate
pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name>
```

Then you can recreate it later:

```bash
pyenv virtualenv 3.x.x <venv-name>
pyenv activate <venv-name>
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Under the hood, the virtual environment is just a directory (typically at `~/.pyenv/versions/<venv-name>/`), and deleting the venv simply removes that entire directory tree.
